note: Static assertions are graded deterministically against SKILL.md by scripts/grade.js. Live assertions require a real repo + gh run; the loop records them as not-run and they are excluded from pass-rate denominators.

evals.expected_output: Recommends exactly one highest-priority issue with rationale, claims it via gh, and proceeds to planning without pausing to ask. Degrades gracefully if gh fails.

static_assertions.pattern: (Do NOT pause to ask|proceed without pausing|without waiting for confirmation)
static_assertions.why: no-args mode must not stall waiting for the user
claiming is a behavioral contract downstream stations rely on
v0 has no fallback when gh is unavailable; skill must halt and ask instead of fabricating

live_assertions: Exactly one issue is recommended, with an explicit rationale tied to priority/dependency order
The recommended issue is claimed via gh and appears as assignee
Planning proceeds on that issue in the same turn

evals.expected_output: Tiny/Trivial tier + Docs type, embedded spec (no SPEC.md), plan.md with 1-2 atomic tasks, and a short type-appropriate report — not the full heavyweight template designed for Standard code changes.

static_assertions.why: a one-file docs fix must be classifiable below Standard
docs issues need a Docs classification path
small tasks must skip SPEC.md and embed the spec (Tiny/Trivial vocabulary)
user: the issue is the star of the show — template must open with the issue before skill/classification talk
same fixed report shape for every issue type is the flagged failure mode
user: the requirements section must be short bullets, not prose paragraphs
user: quality-guardrail talk is replaced by a plain 'how do we verify' section tied to the issue's problem
user: each plan task must state how it answers the issue's requirement — not standalone machinery talk

static_assertions.pattern: (Ground it in evidence|No evidence.{0,12}no proposal|מבוססת ראיות)
static_assertions.why: user: improvement proposals must cite issue text or code location — no proposals in the air
user: the proposal is accepted by default and dropped only on explicit operator rejection
v0 template is ~60 lines of boilerplate; delivery must be tight

live_assertions: Size tier stated is Tiny/Trivial with rationale
No SPEC.md created for a Trivial task; spec embedded in plan
Report opens with the issue title and what it demands, in everyday Hebrew
Report does not enumerate planning machinery (skill lists) ahead of the issue content

evals.prompt: "Find and fix the flaky login test" (no station invocation)
evals.expected_output: The agent just fixes the bug normally. The station-II skill must not trigger: no Hebrew station report, no CONSTRAINTS.md/plan.md ceremony, no issue claiming.

static_assertions.why: L1 description must scope the skill to issue-planning so it does not hijack ordinary coding requests
a catch-all trigger wording would make the skill fire on unrelated work

live_assertions: No station report (Hebrew template) is produced
No CONSTRAINTS.md / tasks/plan.md artifacts are created
No gh issue claim is attempted

evals.expected_output: Skill halts the issue-dependent steps, says what failed in plain language, asks for the issue number/title or a fix, and never fabricates issue content or a plan from missing data.

static_assertions.why: edge case must be covered in the spec, not left to improvisation
fabricating issue content from a failed fetch is the worst-case outcome and must be forbidden explicitly

live_assertions: Output names the gh failure instead of pretending the issue was read
Output asks for the issue number/title or an auth fix
No tasks/plan.md or CONSTRAINTS.md is written from imagined content
